Ἀράμ.long: Ram, son of Hezron and father of Amminadab.
Ἀράμ.as:
Ἀράμ indec. (Heb. רָם),
Aram: Mt 1:3, 4, Lk 3:33 (R, txt., WH, Ἀρνεί).†

ἀρχιερεύς.sd: the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest
ἀρχιερεύς.kj: chief (high) priest, chief of the priests
ἀρχιερεύς.as:
ἀρχ-ιερεύς, -έως, ὁ,
[in LXX for כֹּהֵן, הַגָּדוֹלכּ״, הָרֹאשׁכּ״;]
1.high-priest: Mk 2:2614:47, al.; of Christ: He 2:173:1, al.
2. In pl., chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families: Mt 2:4, Mk 8:31, al. (Cremer, 294; DCG, i, 297 f.; MM, s.v.).

Ἀρχέλαος.long: Archelaus, Herod Archelaus, son and successor of Herod I, reigned over Judea from 4 B.C. to A.D. 6 and died before A.D. 18.
Ἀρχέλαος.as:
Ἀρχέλαος, -ου, ὁ,
Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, King of Judæa, Samaria and Idumæa: Mt 2:22.†

ἄρτι.long: now, just now, at this moment.
ἄρτι.kj: this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present
ἄρτι.der: adverb from a derivative of G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)) through the idea of suspension;
ἄρτι.as:
ἄρτι,
adv.,
[in LXX: Da LXX 9:2210:11 (עַתָּה), al.;]
adv., of coincidence, denoting strictly present time, as contrasted with past or future,
just, just now, this moment: Mt 3:159:1826:53, Jo 13:7, Ga 4:20, I Th 3:6 (v. Lft., Notes, 44; Milligan, in l.), Re 12:10; opp. to past time, Jo 9:19, 2513:33, I Co 16:7, Ga 1:9, 10; to future, Jo 13:3716:12, 31, I Co 13:12, II Th 2:7, I Pe 1:6, 8; ἄχρι τῆς ἄ. ὥρας, I Co 4:11; ἕως ἄ., Mt 11:12, Jo 2:105:1716:24, I Co 4:138:715:6, I Jo 2:9; ἀπ᾽ ἄ., v.s. ἀπάρτι (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 70 f; MM, s.v.).†
SYN.: νῦν, now, "the objective, immediate present; ἤδη, now, already, "the subjective present, with a suggested reference to some other time or to some expectation". (Thayer, 75.)

ἄρτος.as:
ἄρτος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for לֶחֶם;]
bread, a loaf: Mt 4:3, 4, Mk 3:20, al.; ἄρτοι τ. προθέσεως, bread of the setting forth, i.e. the shewbread. Metaph., ὁ ἄ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. ζωῆς, ref. to Christ, Jo 6:33, 35; in general, food: Mt 6:11, al.; ἄ. φαγεῖν (Heb. אֲכֹל לֶחֶם), to eat (MM, s.v.), Lu 14:1, al.

ἄρχω.sd: to be first (in political rank or power)
ἄρχω.as:
ἄρχω,
[in LXX for חלל, משׁל, etc.;]
1.to begin.
2.to rule (v. DCG, ii, 538b.): c. gen., Mk 10:42, Ro 15:12. Mid., to begin: seq. ἀπό, Mt 16:2120:8, Lk 14:1823:524:27, 47, Jo 8:9, Ac 1:228:3510:37, I Pe 4:17; c. inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Mk 1:452:235:17, Lk 3:8, al. (v. M, Pr., 14 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, s.v.).

ἀρχαῖος.as:
ἀρχαῖος, -αία, -αῖον
(< ἀρχή), [in LXX chiefly for קֶדֶם;]
original, ancient: Mt 5:21, 33, Lk 9:8, 19, Ac 15:7, 2121:16, II Co 5:17, II Pe 2:5, Re 12:920:2.†
SYN.: παλαιός, old, without the reference to beginning and origin contained in ἀ. The distinction is observed in π. (MM, s.v.). ἀ. is the antithesis to καινός: παλ. to νέος (v. Westc., He., 223; Cremer, 116).

ἀριστερός.der: apparently a comparative of the same as G712 (ἄριστον);
ἀριστερός.as:
ἀριστερός, -ά, -όν,
[in LXX for שְׂמֹאל;]
left, on the left: ὅπλα, II Co 6:7; ἡ ἀ. (sc. χείρ), Mt 6:3; ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, on the left (MM, s.v.): Mk 10:37, Lk 23:33.†

ἀρκετός.as:
**† ἀρκετός, -ή, -όν
(< ἀρκέω), [in Aq.: De 25:2*;]
sufficient: Mt 6:34 (on the neut., v. Bl., § 31, 2); seq. ἵνα (M, Pr., 210), Mt 10:25; c. inf., I Pe 4:3 (for exx., v. Deiss., BS, 257; MM, s.v.).†

ἅρπαξ.g: rapacious, ravenous, a robber, an extortioner
ἅρπαξ.long: rapacious, ravenous; a robber, an extortioner.
ἅρπαξ.as:
ἅρπαξ, -αγος, ὁ, ἡ
(< ἁρπάζω), [in LXX: Ge 49:27 (טרף)*;]
rapacious: Mt 7:15, Lk 18:11; as subst., a swindler, an extortioner (MM, s.v.), I Co 5:10, 116:10.†

ἄρα.sd: a particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as follows)
ἄρα.kj: haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore
ἄρα.der: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of drawing a conclusion);
ἄρα.as:
ἄρα,
illative particle, expressing a more subjective or informal inference than οὖν,
then: prop. (as in cl.), the second word in the sentence, Ro 7:218:1, Ga 3:7; ἐπεὶ ἄρα, I Co 7:14 (with another word between) 5:10; as the first word, Lk 11:48, Ac 11:18, Ro 10:17, I Co 15:18, II Co 5:157:12, He 4:9; so prop. in apodosis after protasis with εἰ, Mt 12:28, Lk 11:20, Ga 2:213:295:11, He 12:8 (κενὸν ἄρα), I Co 15:14; often in interrogations, direct and indirect, τίς (τί) ἄρα, Mt 18:119:25, 2724:45, Mk 4:41, Lk 1:668:2512:4222:23, Ac 12:18; εἰ ἄρα, Mk 11:13, Ac 8:22; εἴπερ ἄρα, I Co 15:15; οὐκ ἄρα, Ac 21:38; μήτι ἄρα, II Co 1:17; in strengthened forms, ἄρα γε, ἄραγε, Mt 7:2017:26, Ac 17:27, and more freq. ἄρα οὖν (Epp. Paul.), so then, Ro 5:187:3, 258:129:16, 1814:12, 19, Ga 6:10, Eph 2:19, I Th 5:6, II Th 2:15 (Bl., § 77, 2; 78, 5; MM, s.v.).†

ἄρχων.long: a ruler, governor, leader, leading man; with the Jews, an official member (a member of the executive) of the assembly of elders.
ἄρχων.as:
ἄρχων, -οντος, ὁ
(pres. ptcp. of ἄρχω), [in LXX for נשׂא, רֹאשׁ, שַׂר, etc.;]
a ruler, chief: Jesus, Re 1:5; rulers of nations, Mt 20:25, Ac 4:267:35; magistrates, Ac 23:5, Ro 13:3; judges, Lk 12:58, Ac 7:27, 3516:19; members of the Sanhedrin, Lk 14:123:13, 3524:20, Jo 3:17:26, 4812:42, Ac 3:174:5, 813:2714:5; rulers of synagogues, Mt 9:18, 23, Lk 8:4118:18; οἱ ἄ. τ. αἰῶνος τούτου, I Co 2:6, 8; of the devil: ἄ. τῶν δαιμονίων, Mt 9:3412:24, Mk 3:22, Lk 11:15; ὁ ἄ. τοῦ κόσμου, Jo 12:3114:3016:11; ἄ. τ. ἐξουσίας τ. ἀέρος, Eph 2:2 (MM, s.v.; DB, iii, 838; Ext., 99 f; DCG, ii, 419; DCG, s.v. Archon).†

ἄργυρος.sd: silver (the metal, in the articles or coin)
ἄργυρος.as:
ἄργυρος, -ου, ὁ
(< ἀργός, shining), [in LXX for כֶּסֶף;]
silver (on its relation to ἀργύριον, v. MM, s.v.): Mt 10:9, Ac 17:29, Ja 5:5, Re 18:12.†

ἀριθμέω.as:
ἀριθμέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for ספר pi., פּקד pi., etc.;]
to number (esp. for payment, MM, s.v.): Mt 10:30, Lk 12:7, Re 7:9.†

ἀρνέομαι.long: (a) I deny (a statement), (b) I repudiate (a person, or belief).
ἀρνέομαι.sd: to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate
ἀρνέομαι.der: perhaps from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of G4483 (ῥέω);
ἀρνέομαι.as:
ἀρνέομαι, -οῦμαι, depon.,
[in LXX: Ge 18:15 (כּחשׁ pi.), Wi 12:2716:1617:10, IV Mac 8:710:15*;]
1.to deny, say no, opp. to εἰπεῖν: absol., Mt 26:70, Lk 8:45; seq. ὅτι, I Jo 2:22; c. inf., He 11:24.
2. In late Gk. (MM, s.v.), c. acc. pers., to deny, refuse to acknowledge, disown: Ac 3:147:35; Ἰησοῦν, Mt 10:33, II Ti 2:12, I Jo 2:22, Ju 4; ἑαυτόν, Lk 9:23, II Ti 2:13 (prove false to).
3. C. acc. rei (in cl. to refuse), to deny, abjure: I Ti 5:8, Tit 2:12, II Ti 3:5 (cf. ἀπαρνέομαι)

ἁρπάζω.g: I seize, snatch, obtain by robbery
ἁρπάζω.long: I seize, snatch, obtain by robbery.
ἁρπάζω.kj: catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force)
ἁρπάζω.as:
ἁρπάζω,
[in LXX chiefly for גּזל, טרף;]
to seize, catch up, snatch away, carry off by force: c. acc. rei, Mt 12:2913:19, Jo 10:12, 28, 29; τ. βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, Mt 11:12; c. acc. pers., Jo 6:15, Ac 8:3923:10, Ju 23; pass., seq. ἕως, II Co 12:2; εἰς, II Co 12:4, I Th 4:17; πρός, Re 12:5 (cf. δι-, συν-αρπάζω, and v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀργός.sd: inactive, i.e. unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless
ἀργός.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2041 (ἔργον);
ἀργός.as:
ἀργός, -όν
(in late Gk., incl. NT, -ή, -όν; < ἀ- neg., ἔργον), [in LXX: III Ki 6:7 (מַסָּע?), Wi 14:515:15, Si 37:1138:28*;]
inactive, idle: Mt 20:3, 6, I Ti 5:13, Tit 1:12, II Pe 1:8. Metaph., of things, inactive, ineffective, worthless: ῥῆμα, Mt 12:36; πίστις, Ja 2:20 (v. Cremer, 259 f.).†
SYN.: βραδύς, slow; νωθρός, sluggish (Tr., Syn., § civ).

ἀρέσκω.long: I please, with the idea of willing service rendered to others; hence almost: I serve.
ἀρέσκω.sd: to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so)
ἀρέσκω.der: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of exciting emotion);
ἀρέσκω.as:
ἀρέσκω,
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
1.to please (Hom., Hdt., al.): c. dat. pers., Mt 14:6, Mk 6:22, Ro 8:815:2, I Th 2:154:1, I Co 7:32, 33, 34, Ga 1:10, II Ti 2:4; seq. ἐνώπιον (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 6:5.
2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (v. M, Th., ICC, I Co., 7:32, 33, 34; Cremer, 640 f.); Ro 15:1, 3, I Co 10:33, I Th 2:4.†

ἄρρωστος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4517 (ῥώννυμι);
ἄρρωστος.as:
ἄρρωστος, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., ῥώννυμι), [in LXX: III Ki 14:5Α, Ma 1:8 (חלה), Si 7:35*;]
feeble, sickly: Mt 14:14, Mk 6:5, 1316:[18], I Co 11:30.†

ἀρχή.long: (a) rule (kingly or magisterial), (b) plur: in a quasi-personal sense, almost: rulers, magistrates, (c) beginning.
ἀρχή.sd: (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank)
ἀρχή.kj: beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule
ἀρχή.as:
ἀρχή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for קֶדֶם, רֹאשׁ, רֵאשִׁית, etc.;]
1.beginning, origin;
(a) absol., of the beginning of all things: of God as the Eternal, the First Cause, Re 21:6 (cf. 1:8); similarly, of Christ, Re 22:13; of Christ as the uncreated principle, the active cause of creation, Re 3:14; in his relation to the Church, Col 1:18; ἐν ἀ., Jo 1:1, 2; ἀπ᾽ ἀ. (and ἀπ᾽ ἀ. κτισεως), Mt 19:4, 824:21, Mk 10:613:19, Jo 8:44, II Th 2:13, II Pe 3:4, I Jo 1:12:13, 143:8; κατ’ ἀρχάς, He 1:10;
(b) relatively: He 7:3; ἀ. ὠδίνων, Mt 24:8, Mk 13:9; τ. σημείων, Jo 2:11; τ. ὑποστάσεως, He 3:14; τ. λογίων, He 5:12; ὁ τ. ἀρχῆς τ. Χριστοῦ λόγος, the account of the beginning, the elementary view of Christ, He 6:1; ἀρχὴν λαμβάνειν, to begin, He 2:3; ἐξ ἀ., Jo 6:6416:4; ἀπ’ ἀ., Lk 1:2, Jo 15:27, I Jo 2:7, 243:11, II Jo 5, 6; ἐν ἀ., Ac 11:1526:4, Phl 4:15; τὴν ἀρχήν, adverbially, at all (Hdt., al.; v MM, s.v.): Jo 8:25.
2.an extremity, a corner: Ac 10:1111:5.
3.sovereignty, principality, rule (cf. DB, i, 616 f.): Lk 12:1120:20, Ro 8:38, I Co 15:24, Eph 1:213:106:12, Col 1:162:10, 15, Tit 3:1, Ju 6 (Cremer, 113).†

ἄρσην.as:
ἄρσην (ἄρρην, T, in Ro 1:27; Rec. in Re 12:5, 13), -ενος, ὁ, ἡ, ἄρσεν, τό
(old Attic for ἄρρην, v. supr.; both forms are found in π.; MM, s.v.), [in LXX chiefly for זָכָר;]
male: Mt 19:4, Mk 10:6, Lk 2:23, Ro 1:27, Ga 3:28, Re 12:5, 13.†

ἄριστον.sd: the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from ("early")), i.e. luncheon
ἄριστον.der: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as G730 (ἄῤῥην);
ἄριστον.as:
ἄριστον, -ου, τό,
[in LXX: III Ki 3:1 (לֶחֶם), To 2:1, 4, al.;]
1 1, prop., breakfast.
2. In late Gk. = cl. δεῖτνον, dinner: Mt 22:4, Lk 11:3814:12.†

ἁρπαγή.g: the act of plundering, plunder, spoil
ἁρπαγή.long: the act of plundering; plunder, spoil, robbery.
ἁρπαγή.as:
ἁρπαγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ἁρπάζω), [in LXX (as also ἅρπαγμα) for גָּזֵל, etc.;]
pillage, plundering, robbery: Mt 23:25, Lk 11:39, He 10:34.†

ἀρκέω.g: I am sufficient, I suffice, am content, satisfied
ἀρκέω.long: I keep off, assist; I suffice; pass: I am satisfied.
ἀρκέω.sd: properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory)
ἀρκέω.kj: be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient
ἀρκέω.der: apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to G142 (αἴρω) through the idea of raising a barrier);
ἀρκέω.as:
ἀρκέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for הוֹן, etc.;]
1.to keep off; c. dat., to assist.
2.to suffice: c. dat. pers., Jo 6:7, II Co 12:9; impers., Mt 25:9, Jo 14:8 (MM, s.v.). Pass., to be satisfied: c. dat. rei, Lk 3:14, I Ti 6:8, He 13:5; seq. ἐπί, III Jo 10.†

ἀργύριον.g: silver, a shekel, money in general
ἀργύριον.long: silver, a piece of silver, a shekel, money in general.
ἀργύριον.sd: silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel)
ἀργύριον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G696 (ἄργυρος);
ἀργύριον.as:
ἀργύριον, -ου, τό
(< ἄργυρος), [in LXX for כֶּסֶף (Ge 13:2, al.), exc. La 4:1 (כֶּתֶם);]
prop., a piece of silver (Lft., Notes, 191); in NT,
(a)silver: Ac 3:67:1619:1920:33, I Co 3:12, I Pe 1:18;
(b)money: Mt 25:18, 27, Mk 14:11, Lk 9:319:15, 2322:5, Ac 8:20;
(c)a silver coin: pl., Mt 26:1527:3, 5, 6, 928:12, 15, where the value is that of a shekel or tetradrachm; ἀργυρίου μυριάδες πέντε (prob. drachmas; MM, s.v.), Ac 19:19.†

Ἁριμαθαία.sd: Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in Palestine
Ἁριμαθαία.as:
Ἀριμαθεία
(WH, Ἁρ.), -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Ἁριμαθάιμ, I Ki 1:1, al. (רָמָתַיִם);]
Arimathæa: Mt 27:57, Mk 15:43, Lk 23:51, Jo 19:38.†

ἀρχισυνάγωγος.long: a leader of the synagogue, a leader connected with the synagogue: sometimes there was only one, and the name was in some cases merely honorary.
ἀρχισυνάγωγος.as:
*† ἀρχισυνάγωγος, -ου, ὁ
(< συναγωγή),
ruler of a synagogue, an administrative officer, supervising the worship (רֹאשׁ הַכְּנֵםֶת): Mk 5:22, 35, 36, 38, Lk 8:4913:14, Ac 13:1518:8, 17 (Inscr., v. MM, s.v.; cf. also DB, ext., 101).†

ἀρτύω.long: prop: I arrange, make ready; I season, flavor.
ἀρτύω.sd: to prepare, i.e. spice (with stimulating condiments)
ἀρτύω.der: from a presumed derivative of G142 (αἴρω);
ἀρτύω.as:
** ἀρτύω,
[in Sm.: Ca 8:2*;]
1.to arrange, make ready (Hom.).
2. Of food (as in comic writers), to season (MM, s.v.): Mk 9:50, Lk 14:34, Col 4:6.†

ἄρωμα.der: from G142 (αἴρω) (in the sense of sending off scent);
ἄρωμα.as:
ἄρωμα, -τος, τό,
[in LXX for בֹּשֶׂם;]
spice: Mk 16:1, Lk 23:5624:1, Jo 19:40.†

Ἀρφαξάδ.long: Arphaxad, son of Shem, and father of Cainan.

ἄροτρον.as:
ἄροτρον, -ου, τό
(< ἀρόω, to plough), [in LXX chiefly for אֵת;]
a plough: Lk 9:62.†

ἀρήν.as:
ἀρήν, ἀρνός, ὁ
(nom, not in use, exc. in early times: v. MM, s.v.), [in LXX for מְרִיא, כֶּבֶשׂ, etc.;]
a lamb: Lk 10:3.†

ἀριστάω.as:
ἀριστάω, -ῶ
(< ἄριστον), [in LXX: Ge 43:25 (לֶחֶםאָכַל), I Ki 14:24 (לחם), III Ki 13:7 (סעד), To 2:1*;]
1. prop., to breakfast: Jo 21:12, 15.
2. In late Gk., to take a meal, dine: Lk 11:37.†

ἀροτριάω.as:
† ἀροτριάω, -ῶ
(< ἄροτρον), [in LXX: De 22:10, al. (חרשׁ), Is 7:25 (עדר);]
later form of ἀρόω, to plough (MM, s.v.): Lk 17:7, I Co 9:10.†

ἆρα.g: a particle asking a question, expecting a negative response
ἆρα.long: a particle asking a question, to which a negative answer is expected.
ἆρα.der: a form of G686 (ἄρα), denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed
ἆρα.as:
ἆρα,
interrog. particle, implying anxiety or impatience, "quite rare and only in Luke and Paul, therefore a literary word" (Bl., §77, 2).
1. (num igitur) expecting a neg. reply, Lk 18:8; ἆρά γε, Ac 8:30.
2. (ergone) in apodosis, expecting an affirm. reply, Ga 2:17 (Bl., §77, 2; Lft., Ga., in l.; MM, s.v.).†

ἀρχιτελώνης.g: head of a custom-house, chief tax-gatherer
ἀρχιτελώνης.long: head of a custom-house, chief tax-gatherer or publican.
ἀρχιτελώνης.as:
*† ἀρχι-τελώνης, -ου, ὁ,
a chief tax-collector, chief publican: Lk 19:2.†

ἀριθμός.as:
ἀριθμός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for מִסְפָּר;]
number, a number: Lk 22:3, Jo 6:10, Ac 4:45:366:711:2116:5, Ro 9:27, Re 5:117:49:1613:17, 1815:220:8 (for exx. of mystical use in π., v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀρχιτρίκλινος.long: master of ceremonies at a dinner, master of the feast.
ἀρχιτρίκλινος.der: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G2827 (κλίνω) (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches);
ἀρχιτρίκλινος.as:
*† ἀρχι-τρίκλινος, -ου, ὁ
(< τρί-κλινος or -ον, a room with three couches)
the superintendent of a banquet, whose duty it was to arrange the tables and food (DB, ii, 253): Jo 2:8, 9.†

ἀρεστός.as:
ἀρεστός, -ή, -όν
(< ἀρέσκω), [in LXX for ישׁר, etc.;]
pleasing, agreeable (Hdt., Xen., and later writers; v. Cremer, 641 f; MM, s.v.): c. dat. pers., Jo 8:29, Ac 12:3; seq. ἐνώπιον, c. gen. (Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), I Jo 3:22; ἀρεστόν ἐστιν, c. acc. et inf (Bl., § 69, 5; 72, 5), Ac 6:2.†

ἄραφος.sd: unsewed, i.e. of a single piece
ἄραφος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as G4476 (ῥαφίς);
ἄραφος.as:
* ἄραφος, -ον (Rec. ἄρραφος,
< ῥάπτω, to sew)
without seam: Jo 19:23.†

ἀρνίον.long: (originally: a little lamb, but diminutive force was lost), a lamb.
ἀρνίον.as:
ἀρνίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ἀρήν; v. MM, s.v.), [in LXX: Ps 113 (114):4, 6 (pl., עאֹןבְּנֵן), Je 11:19 (כֶּבֶשׁ), 27 (50):45 (צָעִיר)*;]
a little lamb, a lamb: Jo 21:15, Re27.†

Ἄραψ.sd: an Arab or native of Arabia

ἀρχηγός.as:
ἀρχηγός, -όν,
[in LXX for רֹאשׁ, נָשִׂיא etc.;]
beginning, originating: more freq., as subst.;
1.founder, author (Lat. auchor; so sometimes in π., v. MM, s.v.; Milligan, NTD, 75): Ac 3:15 (R, mg.), He 2:10 (R, txt.; but v. Westc., in l., and Page, Ac 3:15).
2.prince, leader (so in MGr., v. Kennedy, Sources, 153): Ac 3:15 (R, txt.) 5:31, He 2:10 (cf. R, mg.) 12:2 (Cremer, 117).†

ἀρχιερατικός.g: high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs
ἀρχιερατικός.long: high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs.
ἀρχιερατικός.der: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a derivative of G2413 (ἱερός);

ἅρμα.sd: a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare G719 (ἁρμός)))
ἅρμα.der: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (perhaps with G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) prefixed);
ἅρμα.as:
ἅρμα, -τος, τό
(< ἀραρίσκω, to join), [in LXX רכב ;]
a chariot: Ac 8:28, 29, 38, Re 9:9.†

Ἄρειος.g: Areopagus (in Ἄρειος Πάγος, the hill of Ares)

Ἀρεοπαγίτης.g: member of the Council of the Areopagus
Ἀρεοπαγίτης.long: member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite.
Ἀρεοπαγίτης.sd: an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill
Ἀρεοπαγίτης.as:
Ἀρεοπαγίτης (T, -είτης), -ου, ὁ (v. supr.),
a judge of the Court of Areopagus: Ac 17:34.†

ἀργυροκόπος.as:
† ἀργυροκόπος, -ου, ὁ
(< ἄργυρος, κόπτω, to beat), [in LXX: Jg 17:4, Je 6:29 (צֹרֵף)*;]
a silversmith: Ac 19:24 (Plut.; π., v. MM, s.v.).†

ἀργυροῦς.as:
ἀργύρεος (v. MM, s.v.), -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν
(< ἄργυρος), [in LXX for כֶּסֶף;]
of silver: Ac 19:24 (WH, br.), II Ti 2:20, Re 9:20.†

Ἄρτεμις.long: Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus, typifying fertility (she had no relation with the other Artemis, the maiden huntress, to whom corresponded the Latin Diana).
Ἄρτεμις.sd: prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities
Ἄρτεμις.der: probably from the same as G736 (ἀρτέμων);
Ἄρτεμις.as:
Ἄρτεμις, -ιδος, ἡ,
Artemis, an Asiatic goddess, to be disting. from the Gk. goddess of the same name: Ac 19:24, 27, 28, 34, 35.†

Ἀρίσταρχος.long: Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica in Macedonia.
Ἀρίσταρχος.der: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G757 (ἄρχω);
Ἀρίσταρχος.as:
Ἀρίσταρχος, -ου, ὁ
(< ἄριστος, ἀρχός; i.e. best-ruling),
Aristarchus: Ac 19:2920:427:2, Col 4:10, Phm 24.†

ἀρτέμων.g: a foresail, set on the bow
ἀρτέμων.long: a foresail, set on the bow.
ἀρτέμων.sd: properly, something ready (or else more remotely from G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel
ἀρτέμων.as:
*† ἀρτέμων, -ωνος (Rec. -ονος), ὁ
(< ἀρτάω, to fasten to),
a fore-sail or top-sail: Ac 27:40 (v. DB, ext., 366b, 399a; MM, s.v.).†

ἀρά.g: a prayer or prayer for evil, a curse, imprecation
ἀρά.long: a prayer; more commonly: a prayer for evil, a curse, imprecation.
ἀρά.sd: properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by implication) imprecation
ἀρά.as:
ἀρά, -ᾶς, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for אלה];
1.a prayer (MM, s.v.).
2. (as in Homer) a curse, malediction: Ro 3:14(LXX).†

Ἀριστόβουλος.der: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G1012 (βουλή);
Ἀριστόβουλος.as:
Ἀριστόβουλος, -ου, ὁ
(< ἄριστος, βουλή, i.e. best-counselling),
Aristobulus, a Christian: Ro 16:10.†

ἀρχιτέκτων.as:
ἀρχι-τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ
(< τέκτων), [in LXX: Is 3:3 (חָרָשׁ) Si 38:27, II Mac 2:29*;]
a master-builder, architect: I Co 3:10 (in π. of building contractors, MM, s.v.).†

ἀρσενοκοίτης.g: a male engaging in same-gender sexual activity
ἀρσενοκοίτης.long: a male engaging in same-gender sexual activity; a sodomite, pederast.
ἀρσενοκοίτης.kj: abuser of (that defile) self with mankind
ἀρσενοκοίτης.as:
*† ἀρσενοκοίτης, -ου, ὁ
(< ἄρσην, κοιτή),
a sodomite: I Co 6:9, I Ti 1:10.†

ἀρραβών.long: an earnest, earnest-money, a large part of the payment, given in advance as a security that the whole will be paid afterwards.
ἀρραβών.sd: a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest
ἀρραβών.as:
ἀρραβών (T, ἀραβ-: II Co 1:225:5), -ώνος, ὁ,
[in LXX: Ge 38:17, 18, 20 (עֵרָבוֹן)*;]
an earnest, part payment in advance for security, a first instalment: II Co 1:225:5, Eph 1:14. (The word is found in cl. and was prob. brought to Greece by the Phœnicians (AR, Eph., 1:14). It is found in π. with both spellings (v. Milligan, NTD, 73). In MGr. ἀρραβῶνα is an engagement ring; v. MM, s.v.)†

ἁρμόζομαι.long: I fit, join; mid: (the middle indicating deep personal interest) I espouse, betroth; mid: I take a wife, give in marriage.
ἁρμόζομαι.sd: to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth)
ἁρμόζομαι.as:
ἁρμόζω
(< ἁρμός), [in LXX for אמן, etc.;]
1.to fit, join.
2.of marriage, to betroth. Mid.,
(a)to join to oneself, marry, take to wife;
(b)to give in marriage: II Co 11:2 (for this there is no direct parallel. But v. M, Pr., 160; MM, s.v.).†

Ἁρέτας.long: Aretas IV, King of the Nabataeans.
Ἁρέτας.as:
Ἀρέτας (WH, Ἀρ.; Intr., 313), -α, ὁ,
Aretas, an Arabian king: II Co 11:32 (Deiss., BS, 183 f., thinks the proper spelling Ἀρέθας was changed, as Schürer suggests, "by desire to Hellenise a barbaric name by assimilation to ἀρετή").†

ἄρρητος.long: not to be uttered (because too sacred), secret, unspeakable, unspoken.
ἄρρητος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the same as G4490 (ῥητῶς);
ἄρρητος.as:
** ἄρρητος, -ον
(< ἀ- neg., ῥητός, ῥέω), [in Sm.: Le 18:23*;]
1.unspoken (Hom., al.).
2.unspeakable (Hat., al.; freq. in Inscr.; MM, s.v.): II Co 12:4.†

Ἀραβία.long: Arabia, the district south of Palestine.

ἁρπαγμός.g: spoil, an object of eager desire, a prize
ἁρπαγμός.long: spoil, an object of eager desire, a prize.
ἁρπαγμός.as:
*† ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ
(< ἁρπάζω);
1. prop., acc., to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., de Puer. Educ., p. 12A), Phl 2:6, AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l.; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, s.v.).
2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα (Ez 22:25, of a lion's prey, טֶרֶף), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phl 2:6, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l.; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, s.v., esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. Ro 11:9, where cf. LXX; I Co 13:9, II Co 1:9), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911.†

ἀρετή.long: goodness, a gracious act, virtue, uprightness.
ἀρετή.sd: properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence (intrinsic or attributed)
ἀρετή.as:
ἀρετή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX, in sing.: Hb 3:3, Za 6:13 (הוֹד), in pl.: Is 42:8, 1243:2163:7 (תְּהִלָּה), Es 14:10, Wi 4:15:138:7, II-IV Mac22*;]
prop., whatever procures pre-eminent estimation for a person or thing, in Hom. any kind of conspicuous advantage. Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence—moral goodness, virtue;
(a) of God: II Pe 1:3;
(b) of men: Phl 4:8, II Pe 1:5; pl. (Is 42:8, 1243:2163:7, Es 14:10), excellencies: I Pe 2:9 (the usage appears to be a survival of an early comprehensive sense in which the original idea is blended with the impression which it makes on others, i.e. praise, renown; v. Hort, I Pe., 129. Deiss., BS, 95 f., thinks it means manifestations of divine power, as in current Gk. speech; cf. also MM, s.v.)†

ἀρεσκεία.as:
ἀρεσκία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ
(< ἀρέσκω), [in LXX (-εία): Pr 31:30 (חֵן)*;]
pleasing, desire to please: Col 1:10. In Gk. writers (Arist., Polyb.), most freq. in bad sense, but in π., Inscr., and in Philo, as above (v. Deiss., BS, 224; MM, s.v.; Cremer, 642).†

ἀρχάγγελος.g: a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel
ἀρχάγγελος.long: a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel.
ἀρχάγγελος.as:
*† ἀρχ-άγγελος, -ου, ὁ
(< ἄρχι-, ἄγγελος),
archangel, a chief angel: I Th 4:16, Ju 9 (Cremer, 24; MM, s.v.).†

Ἀρτεμᾶς.sd: gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian
Ἀρτεμᾶς.der: contracted from a compound of G735 (Ἄρτεμις) and G1435 (δῶρον);

ἁρμός.as:
** ἁρμός, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Si 27:2, IV Mac 10:5*;]
a joining, joint: He 4:12.†

ἀρτιγέννητος.sd: just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert

ἀρχιποίμην.as:
**† ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ,
[in Sm.: IV Ki 3:4*;]
found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, s.v.); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, I Pe 5:4.†

ἀργέω.sd: to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay
ἀργέω.as:
ἀργέω, -ῶ
(< ἀργός), [in LXX: Es 4:24, Ec 12:3 (בּטל), I Es 2:30, Si 30:36 (33:27), II Mac 5:25*;]
to be idle; τὸ κρίμα . . . ἀ., lingers (cf. MGr. ἀργά, late: MM, s.v.): II Pe 2:3.†

ἄρκος.as:
ἄρκος (Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος),
[in LXX for דֹּב;]
-ου, ὁ, ἡ,
a bear: Re 13:2. (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, s.v.)†

Ἁρμαγεδών.as:
Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַרמְגִדּוֹ), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, II Ch 35:22, Μαγεδώ, Jg 1:27;
Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Re 16:16 (v. Swete, in l., but also Thayer, s.v.).†
